sections.title: Welcome to Control & Coordination
learning_goals: Understand the importance of control and coordination in living organisms.
Get an overview of the nervous and endocrine systems.
sections.renderer_reasoning: Standard introductory section with avatar-led narration.

sections.title: What You'll Learn
learning_goals: Explore the mechanisms of the nervous system, including nerve impulses and reflex actions.
Delve into the structure and functions of the human brain.
Discover how plants coordinate their movements and growth through hormones.
Understand the role of hormones and the endocrine system in animals.
Review key concepts related to control and coordination.
sections.renderer_reasoning: Standard summary section presenting learning objectives as bullet points.

sections.title: Introduction to Control and Coordination
learning_goals: Define control and coordination in biological systems.
Identify the main systems responsible for coordination: nervous and endocrine.
Understand the concept of stimuli and response.
sections.renderer_reasoning: This section introduces foundational definitions and concepts, best presented with text and avatar narration.

sections.title: The Nervous System: Impulses and Reflexes
learning_goals: Describe the structure and function of a neuron.
Explain how nerve impulses are transmitted.
Differentiate between voluntary and involuntary actions.
Illustrate the components and pathway of a reflex arc.
Understand the importance of reflex actions.
sections.renderer_reasoning: Topics involve processes like nerve impulse transmission and reflex arcs, which are best visualized with animated diagrams or video clips to show movement and pathways.

sections.title: The Human Brain: Structure and Functions
learning_goals: Identify the major divisions of the human nervous system (CNS, PNS).
Locate and describe the functions of the forebrain, midbrain, and hindbrain.
Explain the roles of key brain parts like the cerebrum, cerebellum, medulla, and pons.
Understand how the brain coordinates complex activities.
sections.renderer_reasoning: Discussing the complex structure of the human brain and its various parts benefits greatly from visual aids like anatomical diagrams and 3D models, making 'video' an appropriate renderer.

sections.title: Coordination and Hormones in Plants
learning_goals: Explain different types of plant movements, including tropisms.
Identify key plant hormones (auxin, gibberellin, cytokinin, abscisic acid).
Describe the functions of each plant hormone in growth and development.
Understand how plants respond to environmental stimuli.
sections.renderer_reasoning: Plant tropisms and hormone actions are dynamic processes that can be effectively illustrated using time-lapse videos or animations to show growth and movement.

sections.title: Hormones in Animals: The Endocrine System
learning_goals: Define hormones and their role in animal coordination.
Identify major endocrine glands (hypothalamus, pituitary, thyroid, adrenal, pancreas).
Describe the functions of key animal hormones like insulin, testosterone, and estrogen.
Understand the concept of feedback mechanisms in hormone regulation.
sections.renderer_reasoning: The endocrine system involves various glands and their secretions, which can be best explained with anatomical diagrams and flowcharts, making 'video' suitable for visualizing these systems.

learning_goals: Assess understanding of control and coordination concepts.
